PayPal || Entry/Mid-Level || Interview Experience (Full-Stack Software Engineer)
Hello, I applied for Full-Stack Software Engineer position @ PayPal, job tagged as entry/mid level at San Jose location.

Got reached out by the recruiter first and had a call discussing my resume and scheduled a phone screening interview.

Phone Screen Round: https://leetcode.com/problems/kth-largest-element-in-an-array/description/ (Discussed both Sorting and Heap approach)
Interviewer was happy and I proceded onto the next final-interview loop.

Lots of miscommunication from recruiter's end and process was riddled with several reschedules  during the entire process.

Round 1: Data Structures & OOP Design: Standard resume grilling, basic and intermediate questions on data-structures (why binary search has log(n) time-complexity) and other OOP questions and a LC type backtracking problem.
https://leetcode.com/problems/subsets/description/
https://leetcode.com/problems/subsets-ii/description/

Round 2: System Design: Design airplane booking system like Expedia. (Recruiter had informed that this would be low-level but high-level system design was asked in interview.)

Round 3: Data Structures & OOP Design: Same as Round 1 but questions were on Tries, Intervals and basic time-complexity of arrays, hashmaps, and search algorithms.
https://leetcode.com/problems/construct-binary-tree-from-preorder-and-inorder-traversal/
https://leetcode.com/problems/meeting-rooms-ii/

Round 4: Manager/Behavioral: Despite this being a behavioral round, the manager asked me a series of system design questions related to scalability, availibility and specific situations to scale an end to end system to handle high throughput and 1 behavioral question at the end of the interview (related to conflict management).

Recieved a rejection mail around 1 week after the final interview round.

Use of reverse proxies (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reverse_proxy) is quite common in modern web architecture. This problem aims to give you an insight on how they are integrated into online services and a glimpse into their internal working.

You are given a set of reverse proxies. Each reverse proxy can be identified by its domain name. For example it can be www.xyz1.com, www.xyz2.com. Both represent different reverse proxies. Users always communicate with these domain names by making requests to them. Like: www.xyz1.com/users/all

Each reverse proxy is connected to some set of internal machines. Each Internal machine can be connected to multiple reverse proxies. When a request from a user hits any reverse proxy, it is forwarded to one of the connected machines in a round robin fashion (https://www.nginx.com/resources/glossary/round-robin-load balancing/).

Due to certain events a reverse proxy can face intermittent connectivity issues to a machine it is connected to. On detecting this, it must remove that machine from the available list of machines. And once the network issues resolved, it must add it back to the list of machines. The network health monitoring is done by a separate service and it informs these events to the reverse proxy by two special requests (explained in the section below).

These special requests should not be forwarded to any of the machines as it is meant only for the reverse proxy. It is guaranteed that only disconnected machines can come up and only up machines can get disconnected, Initially all the machines are up.

Another thing to note is that once a disconnected machine comes back up, it is added to the end of the list of connected machines for a reverse proxy. Therefore, during the reverse proxy's lifetime the order of connected machines can change as they disconnect and come back up.

Each machine has a log file maintained on the disk (memory is volatile !!). When the machine receives a request from the reverse proxy it appends that request to the end of this requests log file.

Cognizant GenC Python Cluster - Technical Assessment DSA Questions (Dec 2025)
I appeared for the **Cognizant GenC Technical Assessment (Python Cluster)** conducted in **December 2025**. The test had **2 Hands-on Programming (DSA) questions**. Sharing them here so it may help future candidates.

---

# Question 1: Students Passing the Exam

John is a class teacher and he has the answer sheets of students stored in an integer array **A** where each element represents one student's answer sheet. Each **digit of A[i] represents one answer**.

John wants to determine which students passed using the following rules:

1. The sum of the answers in the answer sheet must be greater than the smallest digit present in the given integer **M**.
2. All the answers in the answer sheet are different from all the digits in **M**.

Your task is to return the **number of students who passed the exam**.

## Input Specification

* **input1:** Integer **N** representing the number of students.
* **input2:** Integer **M**
* **input3:** Integer array **A** representing answer sheets.

## Output Specification

Return an **integer** representing the number of students who passed the exam.

---

## Example 1

```
input1: 3
input2: 7777
input3: [909, 3347, 1211]
```

**Output**

```
1
```

**Explanation**

Answer sheets = `[909, 3347, 1211]`

Smallest digit in **M (7777)** = **7**

* **Student 1 → 909**

  * Digits: 9,0,9 (none are 7)
  * Sum = 18 > 7 → Passed

* **Student 2 → 3347**

  * Contains digit **7** which appears in M → Failed

* **Student 3 → 1211**

  * Digits not in M but
  * Sum = 1+2+1+1 = 5 < 7 → Failed

Only **1 student passed**.

---

## Example 2

```
input1: 5
input2: 7723
input3: [9302, 1001, 2, 56, 6]
```

**Output**

```
2
```

**Code**

```python
def countPassedStudents(N, M, A):

    m_digits = set(str(M))
    min_m_digit = min(m_digits)

    passed = 0

    for sheet in A:
        s = str(sheet)

        # Condition 2 (digits must not appear in M)
        if set(s) & m_digits:
            continue

        # Condition 1 (sum of digits)
        if sum(map(int, s)) > int(min_m_digit):
            passed += 1

    return passed
```

Each plate has **7 characters**:

* **4 digits**

Format is guaranteed to be:

```
